intended_object: The object map X ↦ X, Y ↦ Y of the identity-on-objects functor C → D in the counterexample for Fact 5.2 of Mayeux's "Dilatations of categories". I inferred this from the docstring and from how CtoD uses it.
explanation: The definition sends Obj.X to DObj.X and Obj.Y to DObj.Y. This matches its docstring ("object part of C → D") and the identity-on-objects description in the docstring of CtoDMap. It is an implementation detail: the obj field of the functor CtoD, split out so the functor can be defined by pattern matching on two custom two-constructor inductive types used in one counterexample. It is correct, but it has no standalone mathematical counterpart, so generality is not at issue.
